text:
maria: Heads-up — starting a coordinated deploy window for ORCH-433 in ~20m. This touches API, runtime, console, and router. Pin matrix and canary plan below. @kevin you own the router header flip; @sre-oncall standby for rollback.

deploy-bot: Scheduled deploy ORCH-433 by maria. Window: 2026-03-23T02:00Z - 02:30Z. Canary target: 10% -> 50% -> 100% if healthy.

maria: Quick checklist: 1) pin versions 2) canary 10% 10m 3) run smoke tests (api + console UI) 4) header flip 5) ramp. If any step fails -> rollback policy.

kevin: ACK. Will do header flip during canary step and watch router 5xx/latency. I’ll post the exact commands when I’m at the console.

abby: Adding release notes + QA checklist: https://internal.redwood/release/ORCH-433. Smoke tests: /smoke api-basic, console-login, runtime-kv-health.

sam: Console request: keep feature flag `console.show_new_route` OFF until router header flip completes. We saw UI 404s last time when flag on during header swap.

maria: Good catch, sam. We'll ensure the flag stays off until `router` returns green.

--- pinned versions (to be applied before canary) ---

```
api: v2.10.0-20260323
runtime: v4.2.1-kernel-batching
console: release/2026-03-23-ORCH-433
router: v1.13.0-headerflip
```

kevin: I'll pin router and run a local smoke against the new header behavior. Command I'll run: `deployctl pin router v1.13.0-headerflip --namespace=prod` then `deployctl smoke router --path /healthz`.

sre-oncall: Monitoring plan: SLI dashboard watchlist (p50 latency, p95, error-rate). Rollback triggers: sustained 5m p50 increase >100ms OR error-rate x3 baseline OR any >1% client 5xx spike during canary. I’ll escalate if we hit softened thresholds.

maria: Rollback command if needed (manual): `/deploy rollback ORCH-433 --services api,runtime,router,console` — ops will coordinate order (reverse of apply). Automations: deploy-bot will mark canary failed if healthcheck fails.

deploy-bot: Canary started (10% traffic) — ORCH-433 canary-1. Monitoring hooks engaged.

kevin: Observing router: initial health ok. Flipping header flag on canary only after runtime confirms KV cache warm. I’ll delay header swap by ~90s to let runtime warm.

sam: Confirmed console flag remains OFF. Running console smoke now.

abby: Console smoke: login OK, route render OK on canary sessions.

maria: If all green at 10m and no alerts, ramp to 50% for 10m then full rollout. Keep chat updates short: "step X OK". If anyone needs an immediate rollback, post `rollback now` and @sre-oncall will take over.

kevin: Header flip done on canary, no regressions. Router 200/latency stable.

sre-oncall: No alert firing yet. p50 up by ~12ms (expected), error-rate steady. Continue ramp.

deploy-bot: Traffic ramp to 50% applied. Canary-2 active.

maria: Running final smoke at 50% now. Please call out any user-visible errors.

sam: Console smoke still green. Not seeing missing routes.

abby: Release notes updated with canary observations. Adding a note about the header flip sequence so future devs understand dependency.

maria: Looks stable at 50% for 10m. Preparing to go 100% in 2m. Any objections?

kevin: No objections, proceeding to full.

deploy-bot: Full rollout started. ORCH-433 -> 100% traffic.

maria: Rollout complete. Tagging release: ORCH-433/2026-03-23. Thanks all. Postmortem: quick blameless notes in #postmortems if anything odd observed. :tada:

abby: Leaving a short follow-up doc with rollback lessons and the pin matrix for runbook.

sre-oncall: Stand down unless alerted. I'll keep an eye for 30m then clear monitor duty.

kevin: One small note — router logs show a transient connection pool WARN for ~30s during ramp. Noticed, but no user impact. Filed RED-1123.

maria: Thanks. Closing thread in 1h if no further issues.
